mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +12.4% over the past four weeks with minimal variance, indicating sustained lockdown conditions. This persistent confinement suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility by reducing opportunity for out-of-home consumption, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +12.4% in t-0w after +12.7% in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL drops below +8% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility has declined monotonically from -45.7% to -48.0% over three weeks, then recovered slightly to -46.7% at t-0w. This recovery signals restoration of commuting confidence. Commuters returning to transit hubs within one week will increase retail-and-recreation visits during commute-adjacent windows, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week by more than 1.5 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -48.0% to -46.7% between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT does not improve further in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC in week t+1w is lower than the mean of the last four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has deteriorated from +26.0% at t-3w to -6.9% at t-0w, a 32.9-point collapse. This signals loss of outdoor recreational substitutes for retail-and-recreation venues. As parks remain depressed, consumers will redirect suppressed outdoor-recreation demand toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues over the next two weeks, increasing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from +26.0% to -6.9% over three weeks
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above 0% within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its four-week mean in weeks t+1w and t+2w.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has remained stable at -15% to -17% across all four weeks, indicating consistent essential-goods purchasing. This stability, combined with WORKPLACES recovering from -37.7% to -35.0%, signals that employed individuals are resuming routines. Employed individuals with stable grocery access will increase discretionary retail-and-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -33% and GROCERY_PHARM remains within -12% to -18%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not continue rising above -35%, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility at -46.7% and WORKPLACES at -35.0% indicate partial policy relaxation. If transit restrictions ease further in the next week, commuters will access retail-and-recreation venues adjacent to transit corridors. The mechanism requires both transit and workplace mobility to improve simultaneously; failure of either breaks the chain.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >2 points AND WORKPLACES improves by >1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -46.7% and WORKPLACES at -35.0% at t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES fails to improve in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC does not rise in weeks t+1w and t+2w relative to the baseline mean.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has collapsed to -6.9%, eliminating outdoor recreation as a substitute for retail-and-recreation. Simultaneously, RESIDENTIAL remains elevated at +12.4%, confining populations indoors. Over the next four weeks, pent-up demand for non-essential retail will accumulate and release, driving RETAIL_REC upward as restrictions ease or consumer tolerance for confinement erodes.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -5% AND RESIDENTIAL above +10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -6.9% and RESIDENTIAL at +12.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS does not remain below -5% or RESIDENTIAL drops below +10% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has improved from -37.7% to -35.0% over four weeks, a consistent upward trend. This signals gradual return-to-work. Within one week, this trend will accelerate as more workers resume commutes, creating weekday retail-and-recreation demand near employment centers, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -34% in week t+1w
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 2.7 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not rise above -34% in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC in week t+1w is lower than the mean of weeks t-3w through t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation mobility has stabilized in a narrow band (-37% to -41.7%) over four weeks, showing no directional trend. This stasis, combined with GROCERY_PHARM stability at -15% to -17%, indicates that consumer behavior has reached an equilibrium under current restrictions. Without a shock to TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, or PARKS, RETAIL_REC will remain in this band over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC range t-3w to t-0w is -37.0% to -41.3%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds -35%, or GROCERY_PHARM deviates by more than 3 percentage points from its four-week mean.
